summary.name: Transitioning a typical engineering ops team into an SRE powerhouse
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog post by Tom Wright describing how Google's network operations team was converted into site reliability engineering (SRE) teams by automating repetitive router upgrades and reorganizing around software-driven work.
use_cases: Planning a move from manual ops work to SRE
Automating repetitive router or device upgrades
Restructuring follow-the-sun ops into on-call teams
Reskilling network engineers as software engineers
summary.what_it_does: The post recounts how Google's production network operations team, which had grown to about 100 people across three time zones, hit a scaling limit as router counts grew. The team identified router upgrades as repetitive, mundane and automatable, and built a software system to perform them, which later became a model for converting other work to automation. Around 10% of the team then moved to building automation, and eventually the whole team was converted to SRE roles, split into four SRE teams with two-site, 12-hour on-call coverage instead of follow-the-sun handoffs. The author also describes skill gaps, internal training, and replacing interviews with a work-evidence process for staff transitions. It is a narrative case study, not a product.
notable: Describes Google's largest full-scale conversion of an operations team to SRE
Replaced interview-based transitions with a submitted work-evidence process
Shifted from follow-the-sun handoffs to two-site 12-hour on-call shifts
caveats: Describes a single organization's experience (Google's network team) and may not generalize to other teams
Transition took about 18 months and involved significant training and trade-offs
Not a software product; no tool, pricing or downloadable resource is described
